headline: Day two of the squeeze rotated into the wreckage — SOXX +7.5%, CEG +10.5%, copper miners +5.6% — but NVDA fell 4.3% and bitcoin didn't move, so the bid is covering, not leading.
summary: Yesterday the bounce reached the damaged. Today it went into the ruins, and the leader didn't come. SOXX +7.5%, SMH +5.1%, AMD +13.3%, AVGO +8.8%, MU +6.3%, ASML +6.2% — and NVDA -4.3%, now -22.1% on the month, 12.6% below its 200-day, in the 19th percentile of its year. The AI-power complex did the same thing: CEG +10.5%, VST +7.3%, GEV +7.1%, NLR +6.9%, URA +6.2%, ETN +5.1%, all still -7% to -19% on the month. Metals joined — XME +5.5%, COPX +5.6%, copper +2.4%, GDX +4.4%. Asia extended overnight: KOSPI +4.1%, Nikkei +2.9% to 60,476, TAIEX +2.3%. Risk regime nudges to -11 from -13, credit & vol to -48 from -53. When the most shorted things are up 7% and the biggest stock in the index is down 4%, that is a positioning event with distribution inside it.

The front end keeps sending the invoice. The 2-year added 5bp to 4.51% and the 5-year 5bp to 4.64% against the 10-year's 2bp to 4.86%; 2s10s flattened another 3bp to 32bp, the 22nd percentile, and 3m10y to 64bp, -35bp on the month. This is bear flattening into collapsing inflation expectations — 5y breakevens 2.25 (16th percentile, -4bp today), 10y 2.22 (12th percentile). The 10-year real yield rose 3bp to 2.63%, the 74th percentile and +70bp YTD. So real policy is tightening while the mortgage sits at 7.18% (85th percentile), starts are -5.2% and UMich is 48.1. The one genuine repair is bond vol: MOVE -7.3% to 85.98 and -14.3% on the week, TLT +5.1% on the month. Plumbing is thinner than the headline suggests — RRP is effectively empty at $0.25bn, reserves -2.1% over three months, net liquidity rolling over.

Credit twitched, but only where the beta is. HY OAS -6bp to 3.42, CCC -3bp, HYG +0.4%, HYG/IEF +0.4% and turning up after a -2.3% month. The investment-grade end did the opposite: IG OAS 0.93 at z=1.59 with acceleration +0.93, BBB 1.16 at z=1.68 with acceleration +0.86, both in the 95th-96th percentile of the year and still widening on a +2.3% S&P day. That is the accelerating thing that is bad. VIX -22.3% to 19.92, VIX3M -15.2%, VIX/VIX3M 0.9554 out of inversion — hedges are cheap again precisely while high-grade spreads are deteriorating. SKEW 150.3.

Three non-confirmations matter. Crypto refused the rally: BTC 74,699 +0.2%, IBIT -1.3%, MSTR -2.6%, COIN at 136 and the 0.7th percentile of its year, ETH -16.4% and SOL -22.6% on the month. The liquidity beta did not show up. Energy equities still haven't marked crude: Brent -6.6% to 91.79 and -12.3% on the month, WTI -5.3%, RBOB -20.2% on the month at z=-1.88, while XLE closed +0.5%, is only -4.8% on the month, +41.3% YTD and 5.6% above its 200-day; XOM -0.7% and CVX -0.9% on a +2.3% tape is the first leak. And Brazil remains the only thing accelerating the wrong way on a -0.6% dollar day: USDBRL 5.5085, +9.8% on the month at z=2.82 with acceleration 2.16, EWZ -25.1%, Bovespa acceleration -3.92 — against India compounding (Sensex +11.9% 1m z=2.86, INDA acc 2.76, USDINR -3.0% at z=-2.93) and Mexico at the 100th percentile of its range. Underneath the squeeze, the regime is unchanged: RSP/SPY z=3.59 with acceleration 3.28, growth/value at the 7th percentile (z=-3.08), MTUM z=-3.01, HD +21.6%, MCD +19.6%, LLY +19.7% on the month. The rotation is the trend; today was the rental.

good.text: The option surface is fully repaired: VIX -22.3% to 19.92, VIX3M -15.2%, VIX/VIX3M 0.9554 out of its two-week inversion, MOVE -7.3% to 85.98 and -14.3% on the week.
Junk credit stopped widening for the first time in a month: HY OAS -6bp to 3.42, CCC -3bp, HYG +0.4%, HYG/IEF +0.4% and turning up, BKLN at the 96th percentile of its range.
Breadth is not a one-day story: equal-weight +3.7% on the month against SPX -3.3%, RSP/SPY z=3.59 with acceleration 3.28, IWM +3.2% and MDY +3.2% today, small caps/S&P z=1.53.

The labor and demand data are not cracking: claims 189k (0th percentile, -14.5% y/y), unemployment 4.1% and falling, JOLTS +4.6%, retail sales +6.3% y/y, industrial production +2.2%, capacity utilization at a 52-week high. Growth pulse +7.
Dollar weakness was broad and funded the rally: DXY -0.6% to 101.72, EURUSD +0.7%, AUDUSD +0.8%, GBPUSD +0.6%, USDKRW -1.2%, USDINR -0.6%, EM FX basket +0.4% and turning up.
The consumer/rate-sensitive leadership kept compounding through the squeeze: HD +21.6% 1m (z=2.97), MCD +19.6% (z=3.79, acc 3.61), ITB +17.3%, UPS +17.3%, XRT/SPY z=2.82, LLY +19.7%.

bad.text: NVDA fell 4.3% while SMH rose 5.1% and SOXX 7.5% — the index's largest weight is distributing into the cover, -22.1% on the month, 19th percentile, 12.6% below its 200-day. Semis/S&P is still z=-2.7 and rolling over.

Investment-grade credit is widening faster, not slower: IG OAS 0.93 at z=1.59 with acceleration +0.93, BBB 1.16 at z=1.68 with acceleration +0.86, both at the 95th-96th percentile of the year on a +2.3% S&P day.

The curve bear-flattened again into disinflation: 2y +5bp to 4.51%, 5y +5bp to 4.64%, 2s10s -3bp to 32bp (22nd percentile), while 5y breakevens fell to 2.25 (16th pct) and the 10y real yield rose to 2.63% (74th pct). Cuts are being removed, not growth added.
Crypto did not participate: BTC +0.2% at 74,699 (-10.7% 1m), IBIT -1.3%, MSTR -2.6%, COIN at the 0.7th percentile of its 52-week range, ETH -16.4% and SOL -22.6% on the month.

Energy equities still refuse to mark the crude break: Brent -6.6% to 91.79 (-12.3% 1m), WTI -5.3%, gasoline -20.2% 1m at z=-1.88, versus XLE +0.5% today, only -4.8% on the month and 5.6% above its 200-day.
Brazil is the sole asset accelerating the wrong way on a down-dollar day: USDBRL +9.8% on the month at z=2.82 with acceleration 2.16, EWZ -25.1% (acc -3.39), Bovespa acceleration -3.92.

trades.name: Short Brazil, long Mexico
trades.line: Short EWZ vs long EWW: BRL z=2.8 on a down-dollar tape
trades.expr: Short EWZ, long EWW, dollar-for-dollar 1:1. Overlay or substitute: long 3-month USDBRL calls struck ~5.75.
trades.thesis: Every EM proxy improved today except Brazil. USDBRL 5.5085 is +9.8% on the month at z=2.82 with acceleration 2.16 while DXY fell 0.6%, USDMXN fell 0.6% and the EM FX basket rose 0.4%. EWZ is -25.1% on the month at z=-3.31 with acceleration -3.39; Bovespa acceleration -3.92. Mexico is the mirror: IPC at the 100th percentile of its 52-week range, EWW +7.8% on the month with relative strength turning up and 2.5% above its 200-day.
trades.trigger: On a broad dollar-down session BRL still weakened 0.1%; idiosyncratic stress, not dollar beta.
trades.stop: USDBRL back under 5.20, or EWZ relative strength vs the S&P turning up two weeks running; also exit if MXX loses its 200-day (currently 6.3% above).
trades.target: 10-12% on the pair over three months.

trades.name: Fade the semiconductor squeeze
trades.line: Short SMH into +7.5% SOXX day as NVDA falls 4.3%
trades.expr: December SMH 470/430 put spreads, or short SMH against a 1x long SPY leg to isolate the relative call.
trades.thesis: A one-day +7.5% in SOXX off a month at z=-2.36 is mechanical short covering, and the leader is not confirming it: NVDA -4.3% today, -22.1% on the month, 19th percentile, 12.6% below its 200-day. AVGO is in the 15th percentile, MU -28.7% on the month, SMH/SPY z=-2.7 and rolling over at the 37th percentile. Money is leaving this complex for breadth (RSP/SPY z=3.59) and value (growth/value at the 7th percentile).
trades.trigger: The divergence itself — SMH +5.1%, SOXX +7.5%, AMD +13.3% while NVDA printed -4.3%.
trades.stop: NVDA closing back above its 200-day, or SMH/SPY turning up through its one-month downtrend on two consecutive weekly closes.
trades.target: SMH ~440 (-10%); SMH/SPY to fresh lows below 0.60.

trades.name: Energy equities mark to crude
trades.line: Short XLE: Brent -12.3% on the month, XLE only -4.8%
trades.expr: Short XLE outright or buy December 60 puts; optionally pair against a 0.5x long XOP to isolate the megacap lag.
trades.thesis: The crude break is now four weeks old and the equity has not paid for it. Brent 91.79 is -6.6% today and -12.3% on the month, WTI -5.3%, RBOB -20.2% on the month at z=-1.88 and 13.8% below its 200-day. XLE is still +41.3% YTD, 5.6% above its 200-day and down only 4.8% on the month. With copper up 2.4%, this is supply and margin, not a demand shock the sector can grow out of.
trades.trigger: XLE closed +0.5% and XOM -0.7%, CVX -0.9% on a day the S&P rose 2.3% — the first relative leak.
trades.stop: Brent reclaiming 100, or XLE relative strength vs the S&P (now +6.1% on three months) making a new high.

trades.name: Re-buy protection at VIX 20
trades.line: Buy SPX downside: VIX 19.9 after -22% while IG spreads widen
trades.expr: December SPY 735/700 put spreads, part-funded by selling the 780 calls; or December VIX 22/30 call spreads.
trades.thesis: The two sides of the market disagree. Equity vol has fully normalized — VIX -22.3% to 19.92, VIX3M -15.2%, term structure 0.9554 out of inversion — but high-grade credit is still deteriorating with positive acceleration: IG OAS 0.93 (z=1.59, acc +0.93), BBB 1.16 (z=1.68, acc +0.86), both near 52-week wides. HY at 3.42 is still the 93rd percentile despite today's 6bp tightening, and SKEW is 150.3. Hedges have not been this cheap since the drawdown began.
trades.trigger: A 22% single-day VIX collapse with the front end simultaneously repricing 5bp higher at the 2y and 5y.
trades.stop: IG and BBB OAS tightening more than 10bp from here with HYG/IEF breaking out above its 50-day — then the all-clear is genuine and the hedge comes off.

trades.name: India versus the EM index
trades.line: Long INDA vs short EEM: rupee at z=-2.9, Sensex z=2.9
trades.expr: Long INDA, short EEM, beta-matched roughly 1:1.
trades.thesis: India is the only large EM compounding rather than bouncing. Sensex +11.9% on the month at z=2.86 with acceleration 2.66, INDA +11.7% with acceleration 2.76 and relative strength +15.5%, driven by USDINR -3.0% at z=-2.93. EEM is -8.6% on the month at z=-1.83 and EEM/SPY sits at the 15th percentile, dragged by Korea (-19.8% 1m), Taiwan (-16.3%) and Brazil (-25.1%) — the short leg is concentrated in exactly the semis-and-BRL beta that just squeezed.
trades.trigger: EEM's +2.9% today was pure semiconductor beta (EWT +7.2%, EWY +3.7%) while INDA added 1.0% on fundamentals — best entry on the short leg in two weeks.
trades.stop: USDINR back above 96, or INDA relative strength rolling over while EEM/SPY reclaims its 200-day (now 7.5% above).

trades.name: Breadth over the index leaders
trades.line: Long RSP vs short QQQ: RSP/SPY z=3.6, QQQ/SPY 18th pctile
trades.expr: Long RSP, short QQQ, equal dollars; roll monthly.
trades.thesis: The leadership transfer is a regime, not a week. Equal weight is +3.7% on the month while the S&P is -3.3%; RSP/SPY z=3.59 with acceleration 3.28. QQQ/SPY is -6.5% on the month at z=-2.57, rolling over, 18th percentile. Growth/value z=-3.08 at the 7th percentile, MTUM z=-3.01, high-beta/low-vol -18.6% on the month. Beneath it, the new leaders are real businesses re-rating: HD +21.6%, MCD +19.6%, LLY +19.7%, XLV z=2.40, financials relative strength +9.6%.
trades.trigger: QQQ +3.5% today hands the short leg its best entry since the unwind started.
trades.stop: QQQ/SPY reclaiming 0.93 with semis relative strength turning up, or RSP/SPY closing back below its 200-day (3.0% lower).

trades.name: 2s10s steepener
trades.line: Steepener: 2s10s 32bp, 22nd pctile, as cuts get priced out
trades.expr: Long 2-year futures (ZT) versus short 10-year (ZN), DV01-matched; cash version long SHY versus short IEF.
trades.thesis: The market has removed easing while inflation expectations collapse. 2y +5bp to 4.51% and 5y +5bp to 4.64% against 10y +2bp; 2s10s -12bp on the month to 32bp at the 22nd percentile, 3m10y -35bp on the month. Meanwhile 5y breakevens are 2.25 (16th percentile), 10y 2.22 (12th percentile) and the 10y real yield is 2.63% at the 74th percentile — policy is tightening in real terms into a housing stall (mortgage 7.18%, starts -5.2%, permits -0.4%, UMich 48.1). When the Fed re-engages, the front end moves first and the curve resteepens violently.
trades.trigger: Today's bear flattening plus MOVE -7.3% to 85.98, which makes owning curve optionality and futures structure cheap.
trades.stop: 2s10s through 20bp, or 5y breakevens back above 2.40 (the front end then rises for the right reason).
